A simple 'each storey is k times the one below' rule is wrong for this building.

plates.notes: Pairs with the dimensioned section, plate 76 - same building, so the two are mutually validating. Independent checks that came out right: predicted floor levels from plate 76's printed ladder land within ~0.2 m of every measured sill/head on this plate; total height 22.6 m here vs 22.77 m printed there. Composition: a 5-bay central avant-corps (uniform 2.28 m pitch, continuous balconies, atlantes at 1er) flanked by 1-bay wings set 2.6 m out, giving 7 windows across an 18.8 m facade. The 2e etage has the tallest windows (h/w 2.51), the 4e the squattest (2.03) - opening slenderness tracks storey height.

plates.notes: The plate named in the project brief. Extremely dense engraving - the facade is rusticated and carved edge to edge, so automatic edge detection fails and the interior floor lines are not drawn. Widths, the cornice, the roof top and the porte-cochere are solid; STOREY HEIGHTS ARE UNCERTAIN because the floor datum has to be inferred from balcony rails and entablature bands rather than read off a drawn line. Note the very low comble ratio (0.117) compared with 125 Champs-Elysees (0.180) - roof share is not a constant across Premiere Classe. Ground floor is commercial (two shopfronts flanking a central porte-cochere with caryatids over).

plates.notes: The widest bays in the group by a long way: 3.49 m pitch with only 4 windows plus the porte-cochere across a 14.9 m facade (bay pitch / facade width 0.234, versus 0.127 at 125 Champs-Elysees). Openings are correspondingly wide - 1.22 m - and the porte-cochere is ~3.0 m. This is the clearest evidence in the group that 'Premiere Classe' does NOT mean one bay rhythm: pitch across the six plates runs 2.28 to 3.49 m. Same non-monotonic taper as 125 Champs-Elysees: the 1er (3.35 m) is shorter than both the ground floor and the 2e.

plates.notes: The most palatial facade in the group: five bays at a perfectly uniform 3.23 m pitch, a giant Corinthian order embracing the 2e and 3e etages, a two-storey arched porte-cochere 7.3 m to the arch crown. Window height falls monotonically up the facade (3.00, 2.45, 2.60, 2.15, 1.80 m) and so does opening slenderness (h/w 2.65 -> 1.59) - this plate DOES support a monotonic diminution rule for openings even though the storey heights do not follow one. I deliberately did NOT report interior floor-to-floor heights here: the drawn levels (RdC entablature at 4.90-5.35, 1er sills at 5.50) cannot be reconciled with the companion section, plate 61, and I could not decide which is the floor line without inventing it. See plate 61 notes.

plates.notes: PARTIAL. The plate is a section on the porte-cochere passage: the left half is cut through the passage and two floors of apartments above, the right half is a courtyard elevation seen down the passage. It stops at about 11.5 m - the upper storeys, cornice and roof are not on this plate, so no comble or total-height ratio can be taken from it. UNRESOLVED CONFLICT, recorded rather than papered over: the courtyard elevation here gives an even 3.70 m sill-to-sill spacing on every storey, while the street elevation (plate 25) gives 4.15 / 3.00 / 3.70 m. Both readings are internally consistent and both scale bars check out, so either the courtyard wing has its own floor levels or one of the two elevations is not the front building. I could not settle it, so I have not converted either into an interior floor-to-floor figure for plate 25.
